body_html:
The idea is simple: leave a rental scooter at a metro station such as Cat Linh or Nhon, then continue by train. The sources reviewed do not describe an official park-and-ride facility, station parking lot, parking tariff or opening hours at Cat Linh, Nhon or any other Hanoi Metro station. This article therefore sets out what is documented (which stations exist, when trains run, what rides cost and what has been reported about parking near stations) and what to ask before leaving a scooter anywhere. Fares and parking charges change, so every figure below carries its source date and should be confirmed.

Which stations exist today

Cat Linh is the first station of Line 2A, which Hanoi Metro describes as 13.1 km long, fully elevated and made up of 12 stations ending at Yen Nghia. Nhon is the first station on the operator's Line 3 list. Only the elevated section of Line 3, Nhon to Cau Giay with 8 stations, is operating. A European Investment Bank statement of 20 October 2026 says it has run since August 2024 and that the underground section is scheduled to open in 2027 under the government's current plan. The planned underground Cat Linh station on Line 3 is therefore not open, and a ride from Cat Linh today means Line 2A.

Is there an official park and ride?

None is documented. The parking reports reviewed concern stations such as Van Khe, La Khe and Ha Dong on Line 2A and Cau Giay on the Nhon line, not Cat Linh or Nhon. A VOV report of 18 October 2026 does mention park and ride, meaning leaving a vehicle at the edge of the city and continuing by public transport. One urban-transport expert quoted in the report calls park and ride a chance to use outlying land; the report does not say any such lot exists at a metro station. Nothing here supports a promise that a scooter can be left safely or officially at either station.

What has been reported about parking under the viaducts

  • Bao Xay dung reported in early May 2026 on motorbikes packed in layers under the elevated line. At Van Khe the reporter found no ticket, no price board and no sign showing the spot is authorised, and at La Khe empty ground under the pillars had become temporary parking. At one lot an attendant quoted a charge and issued no parking ticket; that is one attendant at one lot, not a tariff, so the figure is not repeated here.
  • The same report says Hanoi Metro is not assigned to manage the roadway, pavement or public land beneath its stations, so dealing with unauthorised lots falls to local authorities. It also describes repeated attempts to clear the area under Cau Giay station.
  • Ha Noi Moi reported that on 20 March 2026 the city's transport management and operation centre asked Hanoi Metro and local authorities to check and plan the clearance of spontaneous parking lots and stalls around the Line 2A stations.
  • A transport expert quoted by Bao Xay dung said demand for reaching stations by motorbike is rising very fast while authorised parking is seriously short, and that some official lots (the report does not say which stations) are small and fill quickly at peak hours.

For a rider, the consequence is that a space near a station cannot be taken for granted. A lot without a ticket leaves no record of what was agreed, and none of the sources reviewed says who is responsible if a scooter is stolen, damaged or removed from such a place. The March 2026 request concerns plans for clearance, so a lot in use today may not stay in use. Parking rules change, so confirm with the official source or the local authority.

What it costs: fare plus parking

ItemFigure reportedSource and date
Single journey, cash, Line 2A9,000 to 19,000 VND, depending on distanceNguoi Quan Sat, 6 July 2025, on the tariff from 1 August 2025
Single journey, cash, Nhon line9,000 to 15,000 VND, depending on distanceNguoi Quan Sat, 6 July 2025
Day ticket, both lines40,000 VND (weekly ticket 160,000 VND)Ministry of Construction portal, 7 July 2025
Temporary roadway or pavement parking, bicycles and motorbikes (Hanoi decision)Raised from 5,000 to 10,000 VND per visit; VOV gives this in a sentence about the Ring Road 1 area and does not say whether it applies elsewhereVOV, 18 October 2026, reporting a new Hanoi decision
Parking at a metro stationNo official figure foundNot covered by the sources reviewed

Hanoi Metro's fare change took effect on 1 August 2025, and its notice says the detailed tables are posted at stations while showing them only as images, so the station board is the check. The metro figures are about 15 months old. The VOV report does not say when the new motorbike rate takes effect or whether it covers station surroundings, so it should not be read as the price of parking beside a metro station.

Timing and a safety margin

VietnamPlus, reporting Hanoi Metro's announcement on 9 February 2026, said both lines run from 5:30 to 22:00 daily and that these hours were unchanged. From 9 February off-peak trains come every 10 minutes by day and every 15 minutes from 19:30 to 22:00, while peaks (6:30 to 9:00 and 16:30 to 19:30) have a train every six minutes. The same report says that on weekends and public holidays trains run every 10 minutes all day, so the six- and 15-minute intervals are for other days. The sources reviewed give an operating window rather than a last-train time for each station. As advice, treat 22:00 as the end of that window, on ordinary days, allow for a quarter-hour wait in the evening and leave a margin on the return trip, especially if a bike is parked away from where you are staying. Confirm the timetable with Hanoi Metro.

Questions to ask the rental shop before leaving a scooter anywhere

The rental shop is the first place to put these questions, and none of the sources reviewed answers them:

  • Do the rental terms allow the scooter to be left at a station or any public place for the day or overnight?
  • Who is responsible for theft, damage, a fine or removal while it is parked, and what does any insurance cover in that case?
  • What record of the scooter's condition and parking place should be kept?
  • What applies if the return trip runs late and the scooter comes back after the agreed time?

Putting the answers in writing helps, and A Motorbike Rental Booking Message for Hanoi: Copy-and-Send Template offers a message to adapt. Scooter Rental Hanoi: How to Check the Bike First - Complete Pre-Rental Inspection Guide covers checking the bike before riding off, and Returning a Rental Motorbike in Hanoi: A Receipt and Handover Checklist covers the return.

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily at Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội (near Gia Lâm bus station). Phone: 0334 699 969.
